content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation (fallback target).**

- **Responsive locations:** §13 (p0088) gives Garman ownership of all IP in the Work *including Improvements and the Schedule "D" Modifications built for Sparkling*, with no title to Sparkling; §2 (p0028) gives only a non-transferable, non-exclusive, AS400/Authorized-Location-limited licence to "use", with extra fees for other locations; §3(c) (p0033) bars sublicensing; §4(b) (p0042) has Garman converting Sparkling's data with no use limitation; §14 and §16 support but do not cure the data/IP position.
- **Why it fails fallback:** the licence back is not perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide or royalty-free, and carries no modify or sublicense right; no limit on Garman's use of Customer data.
- **Cure (3 surgical ops, minimality ok:true):** broaden the §2 grant (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free; use, modify and sublicense for Sparkling's business) and drop the location/extra-fee limiters that would contradict it; conform §3(c) so permitted sublicensing is not separately prohibited; add one sentence limiting Garman's use of Sparkling's data to processing solely to provide the services. Garman's ownership of its own software/know-how is left intact (element already met).
